content:
sophia: quick heads-up — onboarding paperwing-v1 embeddings. ran holdout recall test on the longtail short-query set; saw recall@1 drop from 0.892 -> 0.820 after int6 quant. anyone else seeing this?

liam: yikes. is that with prefix/KV cache or raw infer? batch size?

sophia: raw queries only, batch=1, seq<=8. eval set = lt-short-v2 (~5k queries). baseline float32 recall@1=0.892 -> int6 per-tensor 0.820; int6 per-channel 0.835.

anya: do you have breakdown by freq bucket? tail often gets clobbered.

sophia: quick buckets: head(>=100): 0.91 -> 0.905; mid(10-99): 0.88 -> 0.85; tail(<10): 0.86 -> 0.72.

raj: that looks like norm compression from quantization. what's L2 norm shift?

sophia: mean L2 norm float32=1.03, int6=0.78. cosine distribution slightly compressed (more near 0.0).

liam: can we try per-channel scaling or a dynamic-range remap? also test index-time L2-normalize to isolate effect.

sophia: did per-channel dynamic scaling -> recall@1 0.835. running index-time L2-normalize (post-embed) recovers to 0.887 (close to baseline) but adds compute on the embed path.

anya: good signal that angle changed more than direction. what about recall@10?

sophia: recall@10 float32=0.974 -> int6 per-tensor=0.966; per-channel=0.969; int6+L2norm idx-time=0.973. so top10 pretty robust, top1 suffers.

raj: so micro-shifts cause top1 flips, tail is most sensitive. ops-bot: please pause the paperwing-v1-int6 rollout in staging until triage complete.

ops-bot: rollout paused for paperwing-v1-int6 in staging — flagged by eng-ml (reason: recall@1 regressions on lt-short-v2).

liam: actionable next steps: a) rerun with index-time L2 normalize + measure latency/cost; b) test per-channel quant + tuned clipping thresholds; c) shepherd alternative quant schemes (nf4/8bit-float) on the same harness.

sophia: agreed. I'll open a minimal PR with the test harness and raw outputs + per-query diffs. cc @liam @anya @raj

--- paste quick numbers ---
```
-- lt-short-v2 (5k queries)
float32: recall@1=0.892 recall@10=0.974 mean_norm=1.03
int6 (per-tensor): recall@1=0.820 recall@10=0.966 mean_norm=0.78
int6 (per-channel): recall@1=0.835 recall@10=0.969 mean_norm=0.90
int6 + l2norm idx-time: recall@1=0.887 recall@10=0.973 mean_norm=1.00
```

liam: neat — if L2-normalize fixes it cheaply we can consider adding as an opt-in per-customer toggle. need perf delta.

anya: also propose running lt-longtail-aug (more extreme tails) and a stratified parity check across languages.

sophia: will run those tomorrow and drop results in the PR. :chart_with_upwards_trend: 

liam: thanks — ping when PR is up and I'll slot a quick perf run.

ops-bot: reminder: tag incidents if customer impact observed.

sophia: noted. will update here.
